chains.trait: Six jointed legs for stable litter navigation
links: Forest floor is uneven with roots, basalt tuff, and deep leaf litter (F9, F28)
Selection favors low center of gravity and independent leg control
Six legs distribute weight and allow continuous traction
Hexapod body plan with segmented tarsi

skill.effect: Moves through dense undergrowth at 2.1 m/s without tripping (+2 speed in forest/meadow).

chains.weakness: Exposed leg joints snap under heavy impact; vulnerable to espinodo spine volleys.
observe: Counting legs on a moonlit meadow
Watching it pivot on three legs while climbing a tuff root
Noticing six-legged trackways in wet soil

journal.en: They walk on six. Why? Loose tuff and dense roots (F9, F28) demand independent traction. Six legs distribute weight and keep balance. -> Skill 'Stable Crawl' (Basic): moves through undergrowth at 2.1 m/s. Weakness: jointed legs snap under heavy impact.

plausibility.summary: Keep six legs; cap forest/meadow crawl to ~0.4–0.8 m/s (or express bonus as dodge/obstacle ignore, not absolute speed). Frame as insect lineage derived from island radiation, not convergent hexapody.
fixes: Keep six legs; cap forest/meadow crawl to ~0.4–0.8 m/s (or express bonus as dodge/obstacle ignore, not absolute speed). Frame as insect lineage derived from island radiation, not convergent hexapody.

analogues.organism: Ground beetles and carabids on leaf litter (independent leg timing, stable stance); burying beetles (Silphidae) for litter + carrion niche.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Dense air and 21% O2 (D10) cause rapid aerobic decay of small carcasses (F28)

Burial behavior with specialized mandibles evolves

skill.effect: Dissolves small carcass in crop, storing nutrient paste (+6 nutrition, preserves food for later).

chains.weakness: Burrowing exposes abdomen; easily spotted by el_resoplido thermals.
observe: Acid bubbling and foaming on fresh meat

journal.en: They bury meat and spit acid. Why? 1.6× O2 (D10) rots carrion fast. Burying locks nutrients before larger scavengers find them. -> Skill 'Bury & Liquefy' (Engage): dissolves flesh in crop, +6 nutrition. Weakness: exposed abdomen to el_resoplido.

plausibility.summary: Diet: carrion fragments and carcasses under ~5–30 g, not adult rondo. Describe secretions as oral/regurgitant antifungal enzymes and microbes, with mandibles for digging; burial pits sized to the animal.
fixes: Diet: carrion fragments and carcasses under ~5–30 g, not adult rondo. Describe secretions as oral/regurgitant antifungal enzymes and microbes, with mandibles for digging; burial pits sized to the animal.

chains.trait: Nocturnal activity and bioluminescent ventral marking
links: 26 h days heat the meadow and dry the forest floor (F5, F8)
Night foraging avoids desiccation and daytime apex predators (F3, F6)
Low-light environments select for non-acoustic mate recognition
Ventral bioluminescent organs evolve for pulse-coding

skill.effect: Pulses belly light to attract mates or calm creatures in darkness (+12 charm, +5 befriend in night variant).

chains.weakness: Glow gives precise position to nocturnal acechalunas hunters.
observe: Mates gathering during evening storm calm

journal.en: They glow under the moon. Why? 26 h days heat the meadow (F5); nights are cool and bright (F6). Glow signals mates without loud calls. -> Skill 'Moon Lure' (Social): pulses belly light, +12 charm. Weakness: glow marks them for acechalunas.

plausibility.summary: Restrict 'Moon Lure' to forest shade, moonless nights, or dusk; use species-specific pulse rate, not lunar phase sync. Dim or shielded ventral organs, not bare high-contrast spots when competing scavengers watch.

chains.trait: Short-range flight and high-capacity tracheal system
links: 1.6 bar atmosphere (F4) provides high drag and cheap lift
21% O2 partial pressure (D10) supports rapid flight metabolism
Escape from ground predators and quick carcass reaches select for burst flight
Compact wings and enlarged thoracic tracheae evolve

skill.effect: Short flight up to 9 m, +3 to reach carcasses before larger scavengers.

chains.weakness: Heavy rain (F8) mats wings; flight is metabolically costly in still, foggy air.
observe: Tracheal flaring visible at segment gaps
Landing precisely on fresh meat scraps

journal.en: They hop on wings. Why? 1.6 bar air (F4) catches lift easily; 21% O2 (D10) fuels rapid flight. A short burst beats larger scavengers to meat. -> Skill 'Glide Burst' (Basic): hops up to 9 m, +3 reach. Weakness: rain mats wings; costly in calm air.

plausibility.summary: At 1.9 cm and ~0.15 g this sits in the flying-beetle size class. Denser 1.6 bar air (F4) raises both lift and drag; for small insects in the Reynolds-number regime, flight is still routine at sea-level conditions, and elevated pO2 (D10) supports the higher aerobic demand of burst flight—same logic as permissive paleo-O2 for insect giants, applied here to short hops. A ~9 m powered hop or glide to reach a fresh carcass before walking scavengers is modest compared with burying beetles that fly kilometers to carrion. Rain matting wings (F8 evening storms) and high metabolic cost in still humid air are credible weaknesses.

Rain matting wings (F8 evening storms) and high metabolic cost in still humid air are credible weaknesses.
